posts.caption:
You moved a booking to make room for someone else. Did anyone actually tell her?

That's the part I care most about, and it's the part most systems skip. Move an appointment in Kairo and it stops to ask one question: email her, text her, both, or nothing. Only the channels she can actually receive, each showing the real address or number. Then fifteen seconds to undo it.

No silent changes, and no working out a week later whether anybody was told.

The rest of why a salon picks it:

Your booking page sits on your own link with your name at the top. There's no directory, so there are no other salons on your page waiting to take the booking instead.

Availability comes from real bookings, blocked time and each person's hours, then gets re-checked at the moment of confirming — so two people tapping at once still cannot double-book you.

And the money stops being a monthly thing. $400 once, GST included, then nothing every month. No per-booking fee and no cut of what you charge.

DM me the word DIARY and tell me what you're running on now. I'll show you the same day in Kairo.

posts.caption:
"$400 once? Where's the catch?"

Fair question, and I'd rather answer it now than after you've paid.

There isn't one, but the number is that shape for a reason. Kairo is white-label — you get your own instance, on your own link. There's no directory to be listed in, so there's no cut to take for sending you a client. There's no shared platform metering seats, so there's no per-person tier. The work is the setup: your hours, your team, your menu, your client list imported. That happens once, so it's charged once.

What it won't do, since you'll find out anyway:

It won't bring you new clients. There's no marketplace, so nobody's browsing it. Your link is yours to share — on your bio, your window, your card.

It isn't self-serve. I set it up with you. That's about ten minutes on the phone, then the work happens on my side.

It isn't free. $400, GST included, and there isn't a second one.

It's also not a demo. A Melbourne salon has run its bookings, payments and customer emails on Kairo since day one, and every screen in these posts is that same system with invented clients in it.

Ask me the awkward version of the question. DM me the word DIARY.
